native_result.query: In which domain did both original and replication studies primarily use student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%)?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
native_result.HypoB: In the Social domain (social/personality psychology) both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects: originals ~82% (82.2% across 667 rows with subject data; 84.9% across 73 unique studies) and replications ~79-82% (78.6% by row; 82.2% by unique study), the values matching the cited original 82.4% and replication 80.9%. Cognitive studies only reached ~71-76% student subjects in originals, and Economics (n=18, 94.4-100%) does not match the cited figures.
native_result.WorkflowB: Agregación usada: (a) por fila laboratorio sobre las 927 filas y (b) por estudio único deduplicando por id (141; primera fila), siempre con denominador no nulo para el único NaN (id rpp.154). Tabla resultante por disciplina — por fila: Social o=82.2% r=78.6%; Cognitive o=71.4% r=83.8%; Economics o=94.4% r=100%. Por estudio único: Social o=84.9% r=82.2%; Cognitive o=75.5% r=81.6%; Economics o=94.4% r=100%. Sensibilidad: eliminar filas drop==True y/o aggregated==True no cambia la conclusión (Social sigue siendo el único dominio con ambos % ~80%+; Cognitive ~71-76% en el original; Economics n=18). Las filas drop son artefacto (118 filas, todas Social, con sujetos del original inconsistente) y no se usan como criterio principal. El archivo secundario (replication_success) no tiene columnas de disciplina ni sujetos y no participa. Conclusión: dominio = Social; las cifras citadas 82.4/80.9 caen entre el corte por fila (82.2/78.6) y el de estudio único (84.9/82.2).

sub_hypo.text: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
sub_hypo.context: Original and replication studies in Psychology.
sub_hypo.relations: Students were the predominant subject type in both original (82.4%) and replication (80.9%) studies. Community members accounted for 7.4% of original and 8.8% of replication studies; anyone accounted for 10.3% of original and 5.9% of replication studies; online participants accounted for 4.4% of replication studies.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).

sub_hypo.text: Social/personality psychology originals and replications primarily used student subjects, with proportions approximating the cited 82.4% and 80.9%, respectively.
sub_hypo.context: Social discipline in the original/replication dataset: aggregation by laboratory row and by unique study, retaining the first row per id. Original subject data cover 667 non-null rows and 73 unique studies. Denominators exclude missing subject data, including the missing value for id rpp.154. The secondary replication_success dataset is not used.
sub_hypo.relations: Student proportions are 82.2% for originals and 78.6% for replications by row, versus 84.9% and 82.2% by unique study. The cited original 82.4% and replication 80.9% fall between the respective row-level and unique-study estimates.

sub_hypo.text: Cognitive studies have lower original student-subject proportions than the cited original 82.4%, whereas Economics has substantially higher proportions in both originals and replications; neither matches both cited figures as Social does.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison across disciplines using 927 laboratory rows and 141 unique studies, deduplicated by id using the first row, with non-null denominators. Economics contains 18 studies.
sub_hypo.relations: Cognitive student proportions are 71.4% for originals and 83.8% for replications by row, and 75.5% and 81.6% by unique study. Economics proportions are 94.4% for originals and 100% for replications under both aggregations. Social is the only discipline approximating both cited proportions of 82.4% and 80.9%.

sub_hypo.text: Excluding rows marked drop and/or aggregated does not change the conclusion that Social is the domain matching both cited student-subject proportions.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity analyses of the original/replication dataset under row-level and unique-study aggregation. The 118 drop rows are all Social and have inconsistent original subject classifications, so drop is not the primary exclusion criterion.
sub_hypo.relations: Removing drop == True and/or aggregated == True leaves the conclusion unchanged: Social remains the matching domain, Cognitive original student proportions remain approximately 71–76%, and Economics, with 18 studies, does not match the cited figures.
